title: How Ruben Hassid prompts ChatGPT like a team of creatives: layered prompts, human editing, free-first growth
summary: Ruben Hassid explains how he went from joking with ChatGPT in Berlin to building an AI audience, and how he prompts it. He treats the model as a team of creatives you direct in layers (outline first, then iterate), feeds it your own data, and keeps a human editing the output. He grew by giving content away free before monetizing.

principles.text: Treat a generative AI like a team of creatives you manage: give a brief, not a vague one-line request.
principles.quote: you really need to understand for any generative AI it's like a team of people

principles.text: Prompt in layers: ideate titles, build a table of contents, then write section by section, critiquing each step.
principles.quote: prompting you don't prompt once yeah you prompt with layers of prompts and then you see what it does and then you prompt it more

principles.text: Feed the model your own data and ask it to transform it; don't use it as a judgment machine like Google.
principles.quote: what it's best at is to give it data and it gives back something really smart like a summary an outline a strategy

principles.text: Don't trust the model for facts or sources; it answers even when wrong, so supply the sources yourself.
principles.quote: GPT is one hell of a liar be careful

principles.text: Always qualify the output with a human touch; AI raises the average, so spend saved time making work better, not working less.
principles.quote: it's not the time to be lazier it's the time to do 10 times more

principles.text: Grow first, monetize later: give valuable content away free to build an audience, then add premium offers.
principles.quote: I have two hammers one for monetization and one for growth which one should I hit first and I just kept hammering a growth at all costs everything is free
